name: Active Ageing Centre
summary: One-stop support centre for seniors and caregivers.
description: [**AAC PROGRAMMES**](https://www.lovingheart.org.sg/programmes) Our programmes are designed to help seniors achieve both physical and mental health. Seniors are encouraged and empowered to maintain good health by staying active and taking responsibility for their own well-being with the support of the community.​Together with our nurturing and dedicated team at Loving Heart, both staff and volunteers, our seniors are encouraged to play a crucial part in designing their own ageing experience. We will help you design your personal health plan **AAC SERVICES**Our Active Ageing Centres offer a variety of services to the seniors in the community with the goal of providing a one-stop, go-to centre where seniors and their caregivers can find the support and help they require in one convenient place within the community. *Programmes marked with an asterisk are conducted in collaboration with our respective community partners:**BEFRIENDING & BUDDYING**For seniors living alone or with limited social support networks.Connects seniors with the community and build their social network to support their well-being.Attend to their needs according to their level of vulnerability.This service is provided by specially trained befrienders.**SOCIAL CONNECTOR FOR SOCIAL AND LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION**Assist in connecting seniors to their preferred active ageing programmes in accordance with their health plan prescribed by their family doctor Empower seniors to self-serve and register for active ageing programmes (e.g. on digital platforms such as Healthy 365);**COMMUNITY SCREENING**AACs will be equipped with a self-served blood pressure monitor and height & weighing machineThis is to empower seniors to take charge of their own health by self-recording and tracking their vital signs results (e.g. via Healthhub, pen-and-paper logbook)**COMMUNITY HEALTH POST*​**A health services touchpoint where seniors living near our centre can get easy access to health services near home.The NUHS community care team offers health counselling and education to aid seniors in making better lifestyle choices to live more healthily.**The CHP service is available at: **Loving Heart Multi-Service Centre (Blk 210, Jurong East St. 21) every 1st and 3rd Monday of each month.Loving Heart Active Ageing Centre (Blk 318A, Jurong East Ave. 1) every 2nd and 4th Monday of each month.
eligibility: Seniors in the community, especially those living alone or with limited social support networks. No specific documents mentioned.

These shared spaces are used to conduct for seniors in the community an array of activities, from exercises to dance to even baking and art classes. All our activities are centred around four pillars:- Encouraging life-long learningn- Affirming self-worthn- Supporting multi-generational bondingn- Promoting senior volunteerismn

name: CARA Membership
summary: Digital platform for dementia support and safety.
description:
CARA is a lifestyle and community digital platform that provides easy access for persons living with dementia and caregivers to connect to an ecosystem of solutions via a mobile application. It serves as a key touchpoint for members, providing personalised support across the journey of living with and caring for dementia.
With CARA, the Safe Return functionality has been enhanced through the provision of a unique QR code identifier for each member living with dementia. This provides Assurance that persons living with dementia can continue to move freely and independently within a safe community, giving caregivers a greater peace of mind.
eligibility: Persons living with dementia and their caregivers. No specific document requirements mentioned.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

name: Care Services
summary: Overnight respite care for dementia caregivers.
description:
What Is Night Respite?
Night Respite is an overnight respite option for caregivers of persons requiring mild to moderate assistance in their Activities of Daily Living (ADL) or persons living with dementia displaying sundowning behaviour. This service provides caregivers with the opportunity to take time off from night time caregiving duties.
How it Helps Caregivers
Night Respite engages persons in need living with dementia meaningfully providing support for their ADLs.
The service not only enable caregivers to take time off from caregiving duties to catch up on rest or fulfil other commitments. It also support caregivers in managing the sundowning issues of their loved ones.
Download the Night Respite brochure here.
What is Sundowning?
Sundowning is the worsening of behavioural difficulties towards the end of the day. Symptoms include restlessness, agitation, suspicious behaviour, disorientation, visual and auditory hallucinations, and difficulties sleeping at night. This often occurs in the moderate to severe stages of dementia, and may be challenging for caregivers to manage.
When it’s Provided

- Monday to Friday, from 7pm (up to 12 hours duration)n
- Transport option with subsidy is available if requiredn
- Government subsidies for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents are available based on means testingn
eligibility: Caregivers of persons requiring mild to moderate assistance in Activities of Daily Living (ADL), or persons living with dementia displaying sundowning behaviour. Government subsidies available for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, subject to means testing.

name: Caregiver support
agency: Apex Day Rehabilitation Centre For Elderly
summary: Support and resources for caregivers.
description: Caregivers face a range of challenges that can be physically, emotionally, and financially draining. They provide care and support for loved ones who may be dealing with health issues, disabilities, or aging, and often do so while balancing other responsibilities such as work or caring for their own families. Caregivers may also experience feelings of isolation, anxiety, and depression, as well as financial strain and limited access to resources. Despite these challenges, caregivers continue to provide unwavering support and love for their loved ones, and their efforts should be recognized and supported. Please get in touch with us to learn more about how we can support caregivers in your community.
eligibility: Caregivers of individuals with health issues, disabilities, or aging loved ones. No specific eligibility criteria or documents mentioned.

name: Caregiver Support
summary: Fully-funded education for caregivers of mental health patients.
description:
The Individual Training & Support (ITS) programme provides emotional support, coaching, and referrals for the convenience of those who cannot leave their loved ones for long periods. Sessions may be through face-to-face meetings at a location convenient to caregivers, or through other means such as phone calls, messaging, or email.

The Engagement to Empowerment (E2E) Team facilitates the formation of community-based peer-support caregiver networks in six constituencies: Bukit Gombak, Fengshan, Henderson/ Dawson, Nee Soon East and Tampines. The team helps caregivers to connect with one another, share experiences, enhance their caregiving skills and learn self-care, in a support group that meets once a month over the course of a year.
eligibility: Caregivers of persons with mental health conditions, dementia, or eating disorders. No other specific eligibility criteria or required documents mentioned.

name: Caregiver Support - ABLE
summary: Centre-based respite care for caregivers and PWDs.
description: ABLE’s Respite Centre supports family caregivers through providing regular quality programmes and services for both caregivers and care recipients. ABLE’s support groups play an important role in engaging caregivers and providing respite from caregiving duties. We also host annual family caregiver retreats and appreciation events to acknowledge the individuals caring for the physically challenged. These activities are conducted to give caregivers a sense of community and to bond through shared experiences.
eligibility: Family caregivers and their physically challenged care recipients. Care recipient must be cared for by professionals before caregiver can seek respite.

name: Caregiver Support and Training Programme
summary: Caregiver training and support with elder-sitting offered.
description: Our Caregiver Training and Support Programme (CTSP) contains three modules and is designed to support and prepare family members and their helpers for their caregiving role. Caregivers can pick up essential caregiving skills and techniques and understand the various resources available in the community. They can also learn basic behavioral management skills to cope with the demands of caregiving. Through sharing experience and encouragement with other caregivers, this interactive training programme helps caregivers find meaning in their caregiving journey and deliver efficient care with confidence.**Understanding Caregiving**Be empowered as a caregiver. Our nurses and medical social workers will guide you in becoming a **C**ompetent, **C**aring and **C**hampion caregiver through these modules:**Module 1:** You will learn useful and essential skill on how to care for your loved ones who are frail, with disabilities, chronic illnesses or dementia.**Module 2**: You will learn about the psychosocial needs of your care recipient, identify how to avoid caregiver burnouts through self-care, behavioral management techniques and effective communication skills. Identify schemes and resources available in the community that will empower you to be a better caregiver.**Module 3:** Pick up useful tips on how you can create stronger bonds with your loved ones and turn your caregiving journey into one that is meaningful and enjoyable. To provide caregivers with peace of mind, elder-sitting is offered to those who have signed up for our Caregiver Support and Training programme. We will arrange an elder-sitter to accompany your loved ones while you attend the training with us.A certificate will be issued to participants who have completed the course (module 1).Training sessions can be conducted in different languages but will be subjected to our trainers’ availability. A minimum class size of 6 is required to commence each module. For more details on the available dates, please call us at 6854 8300 or email [caregiversupportgroup@hnf.org.sg](mailto:caregiversupportgroup@hnf.org.sg) .
eligibility: Family members and helpers preparing for or currently in a caregiving role. Minimum class size of 6 required to commence each module.

name: Caregiver Support Group
summary: Caregiver support group for sharing and training.
description: Caregiver Support Group. Our Care Corner Caregiver Support Group aims to provide relevant training and knowledge to caregiving, a safe space for caregivers to share their caregiving experiences, learn tips and gain insights from the shared experience of other caregivers to enhance care for loved ones and to build a support network of caregivers to journey alongside with.To register, click [here](https://forms.office.com/r/UgwphQd5Lf).For more information, please contact us at 6258 6601 or  tp.crest@carecorner.org.sg

name: Caregiver Support Group and Programmes
summary: Support group for dementia caregivers.
description:
Caregiving ProgrammesSpecially curated courses to share practical tips with caregivers of persons living with dementiaCaregiving Foundational Course — ‘Embarking the Journey’A foundational 5-session course curated for new caregivers. The sessions aim to equip caregivers on:- Understanding dementian- Managing challenging behavioursn- Purposeful and meaningful engagementn- Communicating with persons living with dementian- Self-care for caregiversnHeld fortnightly across 3 months, the sessions are 1.5 hours in duration and held bilingually in English and Mandarin.To register, click here [https://forms.office.com/r
3pCE6bz4C](https://forms.office.com/r

name: Caregiver Support Group (Dementia)
summary: Free support group sessions for caregivers in multiple languages.
description:
Caregiver Support Group (in English, Mandarin and Malay) provides an opportunity for respite while meeting other caregivers in a similar situation to share caregiving experiences and practical tips, learn about dementia, and discover resources in a relaxed and safe environment. Sessions are free unless otherwise stated.

 The sessions are conducted in English, Mandarin and Malay at different venues for two hours, and consists of talks by guest speakers and group sharing amongst caregivers.
eligibility: Caregivers of individuals with dementia or those seeking support and information about caregiving. No specific eligibility criteria or documents mentioned.

name: Caregiver Support Programme
summary: Workshops for caregivers of children with special needs.
description:
You are not alone on this journey.
We understand your challenges and want you to know you’re not alone. At Extra•Ordinary People, we are dedicated to supporting caregivers like you on this journey. Our mission is to provide you with the assistance and resources you need to navigate the complexities of decision-making.
Here’s how we can help:

- Social Work Support: Our team of compassionate social workers is here to listen, understand, and guide you in various aspects of caregiving. We aim to create a supportive network, offering emotional and practical assistance tailored to your needs.n
- Counselling Support: Our professional counsellors provide a safe space for you to express your feelings, find resilience, and gain valuable insights to manage the emotional challenges of caregiving.n
- Information and Referral: We offer comprehensive knowledge and connect you with relevant resources and services within our network, empowering you to make informed decisions for your child’s well-being.n
- Service Navigation: Navigating the complex landscape of services and support can be overwhelming. Our team can help you navigate various systems, ensuring you find the right services and programs for your child’s unique needs.n
- Respite Care Support: We understand the importance of self-care while caring for your loved one. Our respite care support provides temporary relief, allowing you to recharge and prioritize your well-being.n
- Care Concierge Service: Simplifying your caregiving responsibilities is our goal. Our care concierge service can assist you with practical matters, such as coordinating appointments and connecting you with relevant community resources.n

Need some direction about our programmes for your child? Or perhaps you would like to learn more about what we offer here at Extra•Ordinary People and if it is a right fit. Get in touch with us at Extra•Ordinary People. We’d love to hear from you.
eligibility: Parents and caregivers of children with special needs. No specific documents mentioned.
address: 7500A Beach Rd #01-313, The Plaza Block A, Singapore 199591

name: Caregiver Training Programme
summary: Fully-funded education for caregivers of mental health patients.
description: Provides training to caregivers of persons with mental health issues (PMHIs), dementia and eating disorders such as anorexia, bulimia nervosa and binge eating disorders including related mental health conditions of depression, anxiety and OCD.
eligibility: Caregivers of persons with mental health conditions, dementia, or eating disorders. No specific documents mentioned.

name: Caregivers Support Care Line
summary: Support and resources for caregivers and families.
description: Feeling stressed and unsure of how you can better care for your loved ones? Don’t worry — our care coordinators are here for you.They are trained to deal with common issues that caregivers face. Since 2012, they have been helping around 150 caregivers every month to brainstorm practical care solutions.
eligibility: Caregivers of loved ones, including seniors and persons with disabilities or special needs. No specific eligibility documents mentioned.

name: Carer Lighthouse
summary: Two-month group support programme for caregivers.
description: In-person group session *Caregivers *This two-month programme connects caregivers and equips them with relevant resources for support. Examples of topics discussed: - Stress management n- Communication n- Long-term care planningn
eligibility: Caregivers. No further eligibility criteria specified.

name: Casework & Counselling Services
agency: Society of Sheng Hong Welfare Services
summary: Community-based family service centre in Hougang offering casework, counselling, group programmes, and community connections for individuals and families. Supports issues like family violence, relationships, caregiving stress, and financial difficulties.
description:
Hougang Sheng Hong Family Service Centre supports individuals and families in the Hougang community to build resilience, strengthen relationships, and enhance well-being.

Key services include:
- Casework and counselling by professional social workers and counsellors for individuals, couples, and families, including home visits
- Support for challenges such as family violence, parenting and relationship issues, caregiving stress, and financial difficulties
- Group programmes that foster safe sharing, learning, and mutual support, such as:
  • Women Who Lift – support for women recovering from family violence
  • A.C.T.I.V.E. – social connection and wellness activities for seniors
  • Building Resiliency – practical interpersonal skills to navigate life’s challenges
- Community work that connects clients with local partners, grassroots organisations, and government agencies, helping map resources and build social cohesion and belonging

The centre aims to promote personal growth, emotional healing, and stronger family ties so residents can thrive within a compassionate, harmonious community.
eligibility: Individuals and families with challenges

name: Cloud 9 Community Palliative Care
summary: Cloud 9 provides home palliative care, counselling and social support for seniors living with serious or life-limiting illnesses, as well as support for caregivers. It also offers guidance on advance care planning and referrals to community resources.
description:
Cloud 9 Community Palliative Care offers community-based support for people living with serious or life-limiting illness and those who care for them.

Services include:
- Home-based medical, nursing and occupational therapy for people in the early stages of life-limiting or terminal illness.
- Therapeutic activities, talks and group outings that provide social connection.
- Individual and group support, including grief and bereavement counselling for people experiencing psychological distress.
- Guidance on Advance Care Planning, Lasting Power of Attorney and wills.
- Referrals to community resources, home care, case management and disease-specific support groups.
eligibility: Seniors aged 60 and above who live in the Buangkok Green or Limbang Green regions and have a serious or life-limiting illness, such as cancer, organ failure, Parkinson’s or stroke.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

name: Collaborating with Caregivers
summary: Empowering caregivers through partnerships and advocacy.
description: Advocating for caregiving *Caregivers, community & corporate partners *As caregiving needs grow more complex, we leverage our partnerships to empower caregivers now and in the future.

name: Community Case Management
summary: Holistic case management for vulnerable seniors.
description: A one-stop service that helps vulnerable seniors with complex health and social needs to continue aging in place. **Enriching Seniors with Holistic Community Case Management ** At TOUCH, we strive to provide a range of home-based and community-based services to meet the diverse needs of seniors to support ageing in community. Supported by a team of social workers, our Community Case Management service aims to deliver holistic and customised care for seniors. We are the single point of contact for those under our care, and coordinate the support they need to lead independent lives as part of our community. **What We Can Offer** - General information and referral servicesn- Assessment and evaluation of seniors’ healthcare and social needs n- Service coordination and management n- Care plan monitoring n- Counselling and emotional support n- Home safety management n- Caregiver resources and support n- Support with end-of-life matters such as Lasting Power of Attorney and Advance Care Planning n
eligibility: Vulnerable seniors with complex health and social needs. No specific documents mentioned.

name: Community Case Management Service (CCMS)
summary: CCMS provides holistic case management and coordinates community-based care and support. It aims to help seniors with complex needs remain in the community and to prevent or delay institutionalisation.
description:
Community Case Management Service (CCMS) coordinates community-based aged and social care around each senior's needs, goals and priorities.

- Assesses and addresses medical, functional, behavioural and psychosocial needs through holistic care planning.
- Coordinates suitable services and helps clients and caregivers navigate care options and support resources.
- Promotes evidence-based practice and appropriate use of community resources.
- Aims to improve quality of life and caregiver satisfaction, and to prevent or delay institutional care by helping people remain in the community.
eligibility: Primarily intended for frail seniors with multiple care needs that are complex or becoming more complex over time. The page does not specify further eligibility requirements.

name: Counselling
summary: Brahm Centre offers free, confidential counselling and psychotherapy services for Singaporeans and PRs, focusing on mental health and emotional well-being through a mindfulness-based approach.
description: Brahm Centre provides free counselling and psychotherapy services to Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, addressing a range of mental health issues such as anxiety, depression, marital problems, parenting challenges, addiction management, and caregiver stress. The service is conducted by trained counsellors and psychotherapists in a confidential, safe, and non-judgmental environment, with a mindfulness-based approach. The centre also supports caregivers and health providers, offering resources and assistance to help navigate mental health challenges. Sessions are by appointment and fully subsidised by AIC/MOH.
eligibility: The counselling service is free and available to Singaporeans and Permanent Residents. Clients must provide the last 4 digits of their NRIC, demographic, and assessment data for program usage analysis. Sessions are by appointment only.

name: Counselling and Coaching for Older Persons and Caregivers
summary: Counselling and coaching for older adults (50+) and caregivers, offering therapy and group-based skill-building with a holistic, integrated approach. Services are accessible via referral and appointment, with sliding-scale fees and potential subsidies.
description:
Hua Mei Counselling and Coaching (HMCC) by Tsao Foundation provides dedicated psycho-emotional support for older adults and their caregivers. The programme integrates counselling and coaching with Tsao Foundation’s clinical and community-based services, and partners in the community, to offer coordinated and holistic care.

- Safe, confidential space for older adults and caregivers to discuss emotions, worries and challenges
- Individual and family psychotherapy focused on healing, resilience and personal growth
- Group-based coaching to build practical life skills and coping strategies, fostering resilience and mutual support
- Holistic approach that aligns psycho-emotional wellness with medical and social support pathways
- Accessible services, including sliding-scale fees with possible subsidies and home-based sessions where appropriate
eligibility:
• Adults aged 50 years and above
• Caregivers of any age (no age limit)
• Services available by referral and appointment only
• Fees charged on a sliding scale; partial or full subsidies may be available for clients with financial difficulties
• Home-based counselling may be arranged at Tsao Foundation’s discretion
address: 298 Tiong Bahru Road #15-01/06 Central Plaza, Singapore 168730

name: CREST (AWWA)
summary: Community mental health and dementia support by AWWA CREST in Ang Mo Kio, offering screenings, psychoeducation, casework, and referrals for individuals and caregivers.
description:
AWWA’s Community Resource, Engagement and Support Team (CREST) is a community-based, first-stop touchpoint for mental health and dementia needs in the Ang Mo Kio region. It aims to identify at-risk individuals early and provide timely psychosocial support for them and their caregivers.

Key supports and activities include:
- Psychoeducational events, talks and workshops on mental health conditions and dementia
- Individualised casework and ongoing monitoring through home visits
- Mood and memory screening to flag early concerns
- Information provision and referrals to appropriate services and partners
- Psychosocial interventions and practical support to help individuals and caregivers manage day-to-day challenges
- Collaboration with community partners to strengthen local support networks
eligibility:
• Individuals at risk of or diagnosed with a mental health condition and/or dementia
• Caregivers supporting someone at risk of or diagnosed with a mental health condition and/or dementia, or experiencing caregiver stress
• Reside within the Ang Mo Kio service region
address: CREST @ Ang Mo Kio, 123 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, #01-4011, Singapore 560123

name: Day Care Centres - Senior and Dementia
summary: Day care centres for seniors and dementia care.
description: Our day care centres provide a full day programme for seniors who are suitable for centre-based care setting and require supervision while their caregivers are at work or need some time off.Our safe and supportive environment gives caregivers peace of mind knowing that their loved ones are well-taken care of and meaningfully engaged with us during the day.We provide two types of day-care services:- **Senior Day Care: **A safe daytime care centre for seniors with social and recreational activities, meals and transportation (if required)n- **Dementia Day Care**: A daytime custodial care for seniors with dementia with a focus on slowing down the progression of dementia through nutrition, physical exercises, and brain-stimulating activitiesn
eligibility: Seniors suitable for centre-based care who require supervision during the day. Dementia Day Care is specifically for seniors with dementia.

name: Dementia Care Program
summary: NNI provides patient support groups for people with dementia and Parkinson’s disease and their caregivers as part of its community care offerings within SingHealth.
description:
- The National Neuroscience Institute (NNI) lists Patient Support Groups such as the NNI Dementia Support Group and Parkinson Disease Support Groups (NNI-CGH, NNI-SGH, NNI-TTSH), indicating ongoing community care offerings for persons with neurological conditions and their caregivers.
- These support groups provide a platform for peer connection and sharing, complementing NNI’s broader clinical specialties (Neurology, Neuroradiology, Neurosurgery) and community care initiatives.
- The page also references related centres within SingHealth (e.g., Memory & Cognitive Disorder Centre), suggesting integrated care pathways for individuals with cognitive and movement disorders.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

name: Dementia Caregiver Support Group
summary: SingHealth’s Dementia Caregiver Support Group offers peer support, education, and resources for caregivers of persons with dementia. It aims to reduce caregiver stress and improve knowledge and confidence in care.
description:
A Dementia Caregiver Support Group hosted by SingHealth's Memory and Cognitive Disorder Centre provides a safe, peer-led environment for caregivers of persons living with dementia to connect, share experiences, and learn coping strategies.

Key features include:
- Facilitated support group sessions for mutual sharing and encouragement
- Practical tips on managing behavioural and care challenges at home
- Information on dementia care resources and community services
- Emotional support to reduce caregiver stress and isolation
- Opportunities to learn from healthcare professionals and peer caregivers
eligibility: Caregivers of persons living with dementia.

name: Dementia Helpline
summary: The Dementia Helpline by Dementia Singapore provides information, guidance, and referrals for people impacted by dementia and their caregivers. Call 6377 0700 for support and resources in Singapore.
description:
Dementia Singapore operates a Dementia Helpline to support individuals and families impacted by dementia. The helpline provides timely information and guidance about dementia, available services, and ways to access support across Singapore.

- Offers a single point of contact for questions about dementia, care options, and community resources
- Supports caregivers seeking advice on managing day-to-day care and navigating support services
- Provides referrals to appropriate programmes (e.g., caregiver support, day care, training, and resource portals)
- Aims to improve understanding and promote a dementia-inclusive community by connecting callers with credible information
eligibility: Open to anyone in Singapore seeking information, advice, or support related to dementia, including persons living with dementia, caregivers, and the general public.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

name: Dementia Support Group
summary: A SingHealth-facilitated support group that provides peer support, education, and resources for caregivers of persons living with dementia. It helps caregivers cope, learn care strategies, and connect with community supports.
description:
This service is a Dementia Caregiver Support Group run under SingHealth’s Centre for Memory and Cognitive Disorders. It brings together caregivers of persons living with dementia to share experiences, learn practical coping strategies, and receive encouragement in a safe and moderated setting.

Key features and benefits:
- Peer support through regular group sessions focused on common caregiving challenges (communication, behaviour changes, safety, daily routines)
- Facilitated discussions by healthcare professionals with dementia care expertise
- Practical education on dementia, care techniques, and navigating care resources and services
- Emotional support and stress management strategies for caregivers
- Information on community resources, care planning, and where to seek further help
- Opportunity to build a supportive network with other caregivers in similar situations

name: Dignity of Work Programme
summary: A sheltered work and supported employment programme for adults with moderate autism, offering vocational tracks in horticulture and baking with job coach support. It provides meaningful engagement for participants and respite for caregivers.
description:
Dignity of Work (DoW) is a supported employment programme by St. Andrew's Autism Centre that enables adults with moderate autism to contribute meaningfully through structured, sheltered work.

Key features:
- Sheltered work environment tailored for adults with moderate autism who are work-capable but not yet ready for open employment
- Two tracks of vocational exposure: horticulture and baking
- On-the-job support from dedicated job coaches, working with industry partners
- Meaningful daily engagement that also offers respite for caregivers
- Person-first approach addressing post-18 transition and employment challenges for persons on the autism spectrum
eligibility: Adults with moderate autism who are work-capable and not yet ready for open employment. Participation is open only to selected individuals.

name: Fei Yue Community Services
summary: Holistic support for all ages, including mental health.
description: Fei Yue provides services including counselling, healthcare, training programs and community outreach for the very young to the elderly. Various community teams provide holistic services for clients with mental health needs, home care, including decluttering of homes, caregiver support and respite services, and advance care planning.

name: Fun with Seniors
summary: Active ageing and support for vulnerable elderly.
description: Fun With Seniors Programme aims to enhance the physical, social and emotional well-being of the lonely and vulnerable elderly residents through active ageing community and social activities, regular visitation, and lunch pack distribution. Activities Active-aging community activities, seniors outings and festive celebrative events.Lunch pack distribution to selected needy elderly. Weekly home visitation. Centre drop-in for social-recreational and senior-centric group activities (JiaLe@Hope Centre) Activities for wheelchair-assisted seniors with their caregivers (Braddell Heights Zone B RC). Venues  Lorong Lew Lian and MacPherson Schedule Saturdays afternoonsJiale@Hope Centre (2nd and 4th Wednesdays afternoons every month)
eligibility: Lonely and vulnerable elderly residents. Lunch pack distribution for selected needy elderly. Activities for wheelchair-assisted seniors and their caregivers.

name: Gerontological Counselling Unit (GCU)
summary: Free counselling for elderly facing loss or change.
description:
"Gerontological Counselling Unit (GCU) is a programme; serving individuals aged >55; in Singapore; covering the region of Central and North Singapore; specialising in Death of loved ones
Loss of health, Loss of relationship e.g. dispute, change in place of residence, Loss of mobility/freedom, Loss of job security; offering basic emotional support, mental health screening, counselling intervention, family and caregiver support, outreach talks; Fees: Free; Mental health diagnosis required: No; Note: If client has cognitive impairement or Dementia, GCU doesn't provide counselling."
eligibility: Individuals aged over 55 living in Central and North Singapore. No mental health diagnosis required. Not eligible if client has cognitive impairment or dementia.

name: Grief Matters
summary: Free support for terminally ill and bereaved caregivers.
description:
We offer personalised support to those living with a terminal illness and their caregivers who have lost their loved ones through death. Our services are provided at no cost to individuals and families of all ages, ethnicity and religions. Our team of social workers and counsellors offer centre-based sessions, as well as home visitations to support your needs. Our services include:
 1) Advance Care Planning (ACP), 2) Psychosocial and spiritual support, 3) Support to caregivers, 4) Grief counselling, 5) Advice on practical and financial matters relating to estate planning and funeral arrangements, 6) Link-up to healthcare and community resources, 7) Training and education to promote future care planning and grief literacy within the community
eligibility: Individuals living with a terminal illness and caregivers who have lost loved ones through death. Services are available to people of all ages, ethnicities, and religions. No cost to individuals and families.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

name: Home Personal Care
summary: Home care for elderly and caregiver support.
description: Home Personal Care service is provided by trained care professionals to assist clients and their caregivers with Activities of Daily Living (e.g. baths, light housekeeping), medication, mind stimulating activities, elder-sitting and other care tasks. The average price of the service is about $25 per hour before means-test subsidy. If you require financial assistance for the service, please speak to your service provider or the Medical Social Worker in the hospital or polyclinic.
eligibility: Eligibility for financial assistance is determined by means-testing. Clients or caregivers should consult their service provider or Medical Social Worker for assessment.

name: Homecare @ Fei Yue (Home Medical, Home Nursing, HPC+ & Home Therapy)
summary: Homecare provides medical, nursing, personal care and rehabilitation services for people who need care at home. Services are available in parts of Singapore’s North East and North West regions.
description:
Home-based intermediate and long-term care services include:
- Home medical care: chronic disease and medication management.
- Home nursing: clinical care such as tube, wound, stoma and tracheostomy care, medication packing and administration, and chronic disease monitoring.
- Enhanced Home Personal Care (HPC+): housekeeping, personal care, custodial support, and fall and movement monitoring and response.
- Home therapy: physical rehabilitation and exercise training to improve function and reduce further deterioration.
- Nursing services also include health education and caregiver training and support.
eligibility: Services are for homebound clients. Home Medical is for seniors with chronic conditions or disabilities who need continuing or long-term medical care. Home Nursing is for clients with chronic conditions or disabilities who need nursing care or procedures provided by a trained nurse. Home Therapy is for clients who need home rehabilitation. HPC+ is for clients assessed as needing help with activities of daily living (ADL) and/or instrumental activities of daily living (IADL); eligibility is subject to the Approved Provider’s assessment using the InterRAI assessment tool.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

area.name: North East region (including Hougang, Punggol, Sengkang and Serangoon) and North West region (including Choa Chu Kang, Bukit Panjang and Bukit Batok).

name: Integrated Community Care Provider (ICCP) @ Fei Yue Community Services
summary: Fei Yue Community Services offers a range of senior-focused programmes, from active ageing and community care to mental health and palliative support. The services aim to help seniors remain active, connected and supported at home and in the community.
description:
Fei Yue’s seniors’ services help older people stay active, connected and supported in the community. Services include:
- Active ageing activities, social connection, buddying and befriending, and information and referrals.
- Coordinated community care linking seniors with relevant services and supporting caregivers.
- Community mental health support and activities for people with mental health needs and their caregivers.
- Palliative support, counselling, therapeutic activities and group outings for seniors with serious or life-limiting illnesses.
- Advance Care Planning conversations to help people consider their care preferences and identify someone who can speak for them.
- Lifelong learning, healthy-living, social and inter-generational programmes, including support to use digital technology.
- Healthcare and social support for frail or home-bound older people.
eligibility: Services are primarily for seniors. Community Case Management is for vulnerable, low-income seniors with no or low family support who live within the service boundaries.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

area.name: Community-based services across Fei Yue’s service areas. Fei Yue is the lead ICCP provider for Bukit Timah + Queenstown 3; Choa Chu Kang + Lim Chu Kang + Western Water Catchment + Tengah 1 and 3; Hougang 4; and Serangoon 2. Community Case Management is limited to seniors living within its service boundaries.

email: Different emails for each sub-region. Refer to the link for the individual emails.

name: Mental Health Service
summary: Allkin Singapore offers community-based mental health and dementia services, from outreach and early detection to therapy, caregiver education, and support groups. Programmes support persons with mental health challenges and persons living with dementia, as well as their caregivers.
description:
Community-based mental health and dementia support provided by Allkin Singapore, delivered through multiple teams and programmes that work with healthcare and community partners.
- Community outreach (CREST): Raises awareness of dementia and mental health, promotes early detection, provides emotional support, conducts preventive and cognitive-stimulating activities, and links people to suitable health and social care services.
- Post-Diagnostic Support (PDS-Dementia): Six-month support for persons newly diagnosed with dementia and their caregivers, including education on the condition, coordination of community resources, and early planning/management.
- Meeting Centre Support Programme (MCSP): Facilitated group sessions for persons with mild to early moderate dementia featuring psychosocial, physical, cognitive stimulation, and social activities (meets alternate Monday afternoons).
- Orientation Programme for Caregivers (OPCG): A 5-session series (twice yearly) covering understanding dementia, caregiving skills, coping strategies, Advance Care Planning and LPA, and community resources.
- Caregivers Strength Circle (CSC): Ongoing support group for caregivers of persons living with dementia to connect and organise interest-focused activities, with monthly gatherings and an annual celebration.
- Community Intervention Team (COMIT): Provides assessment, therapy, counselling, psychoeducation, case management, personalised care plans, and caregiver support/training; coordinates closely with polyclinics, GPs and community partners.
- Part of the national Community Mental Health Masterplan (MOH & AIC), enabling early, accessible care near home and sustained support in the community.
eligibility:
• Persons with mental health issues and persons living with dementia in the community.
• MCSP: Persons living with mild to early moderate dementia.
• OPCG: Any caregivers (primary or secondary) of persons living with dementia in Singapore.
• CSC: Caregivers of persons living with dementia.
• Service areas: CREST focuses on Punggol Coast, Punggol Shore, Punggol West SMC, Compassvale, Rivervale, Pasir Ris East, Pasir Ris Central, Pasir Ris West, Teck Ghee, Bishan East, Sin Ming, Kebun Baru SMC, Marymount SMC. COMIT is open to residents in Ang Mo Kio, Sin Ming, Bishan, Hougang, Sengkang and Punggol.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses

COMIT open to residents in: Ang Mo Kio, Sin Ming, Bishan, Hougang, Sengkang, Punggol.

name: MINDS
agency: Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore (MINDS)
summary: Empowers special needs individuals through diverse support services.
description: MINDS seeks to empower individuals with special needs through social enterprise programmes, advocacy, caregiver respite, therapy, befriending services for social integration, supported employment, home care, decluttering, training and development.

name: Project Dementia and Caregiver care services (Meeting Centre Support Programme)
summary: A Dementia Care programme offering meaningful activities and support for seniors with dementia and their families, delivered in partnership with Dementia Singapore.
description:
- Dementia Care service providing meaningful, structured activities for seniors living with dementia
- Meeting Centre Support Programme run in partnership with Dementia Singapore, aimed at supporting persons living with dementia and their families
eligibility: Persons living with dementia and their families.

name: Rehabilitation Centre and Respite Centre
summary: ABLE supports physically challenged and their caregivers.
description: Provides Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy and Pilates rehabilitation, with the goal of working towards integrating persons with physical disability back to work and society. Training courses to equip clients with the relevant skills to enhance their employability. Respite for Family Caregivers provides centre and home based respite services to help family caregivers of the physically challenged care recipients. Wheelchair-accessible vans to provide transport at reasonable rates.
eligibility: Persons with physical challenges and their family caregivers. No specific eligibility documents mentioned.

name: Respite Care
summary: Respite care and befriending for caregivers.
description: We provide respite care for caregivers to take time-off for self-care. Our befrienders will engage the care recipient loved ones meaningfully by focusing on stimulating their minds and building cognitive capacity.

name: Respite Care Services (Eldercare)
agency: Islandwide senior care centres run by various providers (see link on HealthHub)
summary: Senior Care Centres provide short-term daytime care for elderly.
description:
Caregivers can tap on Senior Care Centres for short-term care options, such as when they need to take short breaks from caregiving on an ad-hoc basis during the day.

 Short-term care options at Senior Care Centres are also suitable if caregivers need additional assistance when the foreign domestic worker is not available.
eligibility: Caregivers of elderly individuals who require short-term care during the day, especially when the caregiver needs a break or when a foreign domestic worker is not available.

name: SASCO@WestCoast AAC
summary: Seven centres provide care and support for elderly.
description: **As of 1st April 2023 SASCO@WestCoast is AAC (Care)**, this centre is a Senior Care Centre and Active Ageing Centre combined, Active Ageing Centre (Care), or AAC (Care), provides AAC services and additional care services, such as day care and community rehabilitation, in separate facilities nearby. [https://www.aic.sg/care-services/active-ageing-centre](https://www.aic.sg/care-services/active-ageing-centre).
eligibility: Seniors aged 60 years and above, especially those who are frail, destitute, facing financial or family challenges, or living with dementia.

name: Senior Care Centres
summary: PCS Senior Care Centres offer full-day care programmes for seniors aged 60 and above, focusing on mental and physical well-being, social interaction, and support for caregivers. They provide meals, transport options, and a secure environment to promote dignified ageing in place.
description: PCS Senior Care Centres (SSC) provide full-day care programmes for Singaporeans and Permanent Residents aged 60 and above, aiming to promote ageing in place. The centres offer a secure environment with activities designed to enhance memory, social interaction, music engagement, and maintenance of daily living activities. Using the PCS MDC Individualised Care Plan, the centres provide maintenance exercises and regimental activities to stimulate mental and physical health, helping to prevent or delay cognitive decline. The centres also support frail and/or physically disabled seniors, improve their general well-being, and provide respite and support to their families and caregivers. Meals and transport (with additional charges) are provided at various locations operating Monday to Friday, with some centres open on Saturdays.
eligibility: Singaporeans and Permanent Residents aged 60 years and above.

name: Senior Service
summary: Monthly support group for dementia caregivers.
description: CREST SS @REACH runs a Caregiver Support Group to help caregivers of loved ones with dementia or depression to be better prepared at the earlier stage, to find more adaptive ways of coping when the going gets tough and to facilitate self-care. Our Care Circle runs on Saturday mornings on monthly basis. Elder-sitting service for seniors with mild to moderate dementia and depressive symptoms is available to free up caregivers to attend the support group.
eligibility: Caregivers of loved ones with dementia or depression. Elder-sitting service is for seniors with mild to moderate dementia or depressive symptoms.

name: Sheng Hong Active Ageing Centre (Care)@Sennett
agency: Society of Sheng Hong Welfare Services
summary: Sheng Hong Active Ageing Centre (CARE) @ Sennett provides Active Ageing activities, Day Rehabilitation, and Day Care & Dementia Day Care for seniors. It helps older adults stay healthy and socially connected while offering respite for caregivers.
description:
- Community-based eldercare at Sheng Hong Active Ageing Centre (CARE) @ Sennett supporting seniors' health, independence and social well-being
- Active Ageing Programmes: group activities and courses designed to promote social interaction, mental stimulation and physical wellness so seniors can stay engaged and independent
- Day Rehabilitation: therapy-led sessions to help regain or maintain strength, mobility and functional abilities, guided by trained staff and personalised exercises
- Day Care & Dementia Day Care: structured daytime supervision and activities tailored to individual cognitive, physical and emotional needs, providing a safe, stimulating environment and easing caregiving load for families
- Mission-driven, holistic approach intended to value, support and empower seniors with dignity, purpose and joy
eligibility: Seniors/older adults who would benefit from active ageing activities, day rehabilitation, or structured day care (including those living with dementia) and who require daytime supervision or support.

name: Singapore Association for Mental Health Mobile Support Team COMIT
agency: Singapore Association for Mental Health Mobile Support Team COMIT
summary: Community mental health support for clients and caregivers.
description: SAMH Mobile Support Team COMIT is a community based allied health-led team which provides psycho-social therapeutic interventions for clients with mental health needs and support for their caregivers to maintain clients well in the community.MST provides a holistic service to clients and caregivers, equipping them with information to make informed decisions for the management of their condition and support social re-integration, resulting in an improvement in functioning and quality of life.Each multi-disciplinary team comprises allied health professionals and programme coordinators to provide the following services:- Perform needs assessments of clients and caregiversn- Develop individualised intervention plans, case management, and monitoring of clients in the community, in close collaboration with GPs or hospitals for further assessments and treatment interventions.n- Provide groupwork for clients and caregiversn- Home visits for assessment and close follow ups on client and caregivers for effective copingn- Provide care coordination and referrals for clients to appropriate services based on their needsn- Training and outreach, e.g., to raise awareness and understanding of mental disorders for the general publicn
eligibility: Clients with mental health needs and their caregivers. No specific eligibility documents mentioned.

name: Special Needs Trust Company
summary: Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) provides trust and future care planning services for persons with disabilities and special needs, supporting caregivers with structured financial arrangements and case-managed care plans. It helps ensure continuity of care and responsible disbursement of funds for beneficiaries’ long-term needs.
description:
- Non-profit trust service dedicated to safeguarding the long-term welfare of persons with disabilities and special needs in Singapore
- Supports caregivers and families to plan for the future through professional care planning and trust administration
- Key offerings include:
  - Special Needs Trust: Setting up and managing trust accounts to provide structured, needs-based disbursements for beneficiaries with special needs
  - Special Needs Savings Scheme: Facilitates CPF nominations to provide regular payouts for the beneficiary’s care after the caregiver’s passing
  - Case management and care planning: Dedicated case managers work with caregivers to develop a comprehensive care plan that guides future support and fund disbursement
  - Education and guidance for caregivers on future care planning and how to coordinate services across community resources
- Aims to give peace of mind to caregivers by ensuring continuity of care and prudent use of funds for their loved ones

name: Specialised Case Management Programme
summary: SPD’s Specialised Case Management Programme (SCMP) provides coordinated case management, counselling, assistive device support, support groups, and caregiver training for persons with disabilities and their caregivers across Singapore.
description:
The Specialised Case Management Programme (SCMP) by SPD is a nationwide initiative launched in 2006 to support persons with disabilities across all age groups and their caregivers. It aims to empower individuals and families to lead more fulfilling lives through coordinated, holistic support delivered by social workers and case management officers.

Key supports include:
- Coordination of services within SPD and with community resources
- Supportive counselling and case management
- Assessment and support for the purchase of assistive devices
- Support groups for learning and networking
- Caregiver support and training
- Information and referral to relevant programmes and services

The programme is designed for individuals with disabilities who may face multiple and complex challenges, and for their caregivers who need guidance, training, and practical support.
eligibility:
- Persons of any age with physical or sensory disabilities and their caregivers. 
- Persons with multiple needs. 
- Singapore citizen or Permanent Resident.
address: SPD Headquarters, 2 Peng Nguan Street, SPD Ability Centre, Singapore 168955

name: StrokeConnect
summary: StrokeConnect is a peer-led helpline by the Singapore National Stroke Association that provides emotional support, information, and referrals to stroke survivors and caregivers. Trained befrienders with lived experience guide callers to suitable SNSA programmes and community resources.
description:
- A helpline that connects stroke survivors and caregivers with trained peer befrienders who are themselves stroke survivors
- Provides survivor-to-survivor listening, understanding, and emotional support based on lived experience
- Helps callers understand available SNSA programmes and links them to the most suitable options
- Guides users to relevant community resources and the next steps in their recovery or caregiving journey
- Non-clinical, non-medical support; focuses on sharing experiences, practical guidance, and referrals
- Operating hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00–18:00
- Brochures available in English and Chinese
eligibility: Intended for stroke survivors and caregivers seeking non-clinical peer support, information, or guidance on recovery resources. Not a medical or clinical advice service.

- Provides care and activities in community-based centres, working alongside caregivers to improve quality of life
- Aims to build inclusive communities in Singapore through services for clients and support for their caregivers

summary: Counselling and support for addiction caregivers.

eligibility: Family members and caregivers of persons struggling with addiction.

name: The Compassionate Network
summary: Support for caregivers of people nearing end-of-life.
description: The Compassionate Network (TCN) is a charity in Singapore dedicated to supporting caregivers of patients with advanced illnesses.Established in July 2023, TCN is the first and only charity dedicated to supporting caregivers of patients with advanced illnesses using lay helpers to form circles of care, to oﬀer companionship, guidance, grief education and more – ensuring they are not alone in their journey. **What We Do** TCN hopes to create a compassionate community by rallying volunteers, corporates, and community partners to form circles of care around caregivers of people nearing life's end. We recognise that family caregivers are themselves care recipients too – they deserve attention and support as much as those they care for. By nurturing the wellbeing of caregivers, we honour their dignity in caring for their loved ones in life's final chapter. We tailor our support according to the different needs of the caregivers - some prefer to focus on their personal well-being while others request assistance with various caregiving activities. Beyond the caregiving period, TCN supports caregivers into their bereavement phase and facilitate their transitions to a physical world without their loved ones.
eligibility: Open to volunteers, corporates, and community partners interested in supporting caregivers of people nearing end-of-life. No specific eligibility criteria for caregivers mentioned.

name: TOUCH Caregivers Support
summary: Support and advice for elder caregiving at home.
description: Provide support and advice for caregiving of elders at home to support ageing in place. Care Line at 6804 6555.

name: TRANS FOCUS Active Ageing Centre
summary: Active Ageing Centre for seniors' well-being and support.
description: TRANS FOCUS Active Ageing Centre strongly believes in the possibility of seniors ageing successfully in a neighbourhood in which they are familiar with. As such we create opportunities for seniors aged 50 years and above to lead active and fulfilling lives.Active LearningWe create opportunities for seniors to continue to learn new skills and knowledge so as to promote lifelong learning.Active VolunteerismWe encourage seniors to develop talents and strengths and share them with fellow seniors. This can take the form of leading an activity, imparting skills to other seniors and visiting other charitable organisations.Community Mental Health ServiceWe provide mental health education and conduct screening for our seniors to detect early signs of depression or dementia.Caregiver Resource and SupportWe provide information and referral service to caregivers to support them in their caregiving journey.
eligibility: Older adults and seniors in the neighbourhood. No specific eligibility criteria mentioned.

name: Various services (community kitchen, Active Ageing Centre, personalised care for seniors)
summary: Holistic active ageing programmes for seniors in Singapore.
description: Network for people with dementia and depression, as well as caregivers who need the additional support to care for their loved ones. Provides appropriate mental health care and social support networks through outreach and education. A dedicated team of social workers assess the needs of the elderly and link senior citizens or caregivers to the relevant community resources. Care Closer to Home (CACHE) provides support and guidance for elderly aged 50 years old and above, diagnosed with one or more chronic illnesses. Elderly clients' health conditions are monitored on a regular basis and the clients are taught to manage their medication and wellbeing. Befriending services: regular home visits to seniors and caregivers who need assistance and support.
eligibility: Eligibility is primarily for seniors, including frail elderly, those with complex needs, bedbound seniors, seniors with dementia or depression, and their caregivers. No specific age or residency requirements stated.
whoIsItFor: Persons with chronic or terminal illnesses
